title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure built on synthetic media. A generative system was used to place the faces of identifiable women onto existing adult content, producing video of acts they did not perform. The output is not a false claim about a person, it is a fabricated record of their body and conduct, and it circulates as though it were real. The people depicted are identifiable women, several of them public figures, and the harm lands on them rather than on anyone who made or viewed the material.

The failure sits at the hosting layer rather than at the point of generation. The material was uploaded to a platform with a very large audience, and uploaders were encouraged to stay anonymous. Catching it before publication would have required the platform to screen incoming video for manipulated faces, or to tie uploads to verified identities, or a designated authority able to order unlawful sexual images offline. The reports include a parliamentary motion to create exactly that last mechanism, which is a request for a route that the reporting does not show being used.

What is not established is intent or outcome. The reports describe complaints filed and legal options being explored, which are allegations and intentions rather than findings. The suggestion that anonymity is sought in order to avoid prosecution is presented as a likelihood, not as a proven purpose. The conditional sentence given to one man is a single case, and its connection to these videos is not established. The reports also note that parliamentary attention faded and members heard nothing for months, which is a fact about the official response and not a finding about the platform.

summary:
Multiple Dutch female celebrities are considering filing charges after fake pornographic videos featuring their faces appeared on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The manipulated content includes videos of entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disturbing and urged victims to report them. Managers and representatives confirmed that some victims have filed complaints or are exploring legal options.

These deepfake videos are created by placing a celebrity's face onto adult content. Users who upload material are encouraged to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution. Lawyers warn that without government intervention, more fake videos will continue appearing. Deepfakes fall under revenge porn laws and are illegal. Victims can file police reports, which may lead to website takedowns, or pursue other options including class action lawsuits and complaints to data protection authorities. One case resulted in a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours of community service.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
